_doc: Medium batch m04 themed pass (Opus): 12 birds. Every creature has its own signature motif (module claude/pf-anim/motifs/medium_m04.js, 32 motifs); one small motif reused where truly the same (grouse-whirr for the ptarmigan flush). All 8 pieces per creature carry a hand note. Corvid siblings (carrion-crow, jungle-crow) share corvid-caw and crow-quill as secondary motifs with different palette and speed.

snow-owl-fledgling.notes: A big grey ball of down with huge yellow eyes: clumsy, wobbling, feathered feet too big for it; it hisses and screeches when cross (enrage) in tundra snow.

p.b0: Fluff-Beak Peck: grey fluffballs teeter off the edge beak first, yellow eyes blinking

b1.n: Clumsy Foot Grab: big feathered feet lunge out and the dark talons open to grab

b2.n: Fluffed Wing Bluff: the owlets line the edge and puff up twice their size, down puffs swelling

b3.n: Awkward Hop Away: fluffballs hop out in all directions and wobble back, snow knocked loose

u0.n: Fluff Pounce: a heavy fluffball slams out and drops back, snow puffing up; the chain bounces to the next piece

u1.n: Fledgling Screech: owlet heads gape and jagged screech marks shoot off the edge; sound rings carry it on

u2.n: Down Wall: a wall of grey down tufts bristles up along the edge, snowflakes caught in it

u3.n: Clumsy Feet: feathered feet stamp out and back, talons splayed, snow kicked up

carrion-crow.notes: Clever black carrion crow on fields and crags: hops two-footed with a sly pale eye, mobs in a cawing gang and steals hats; aims two ways at once.

b0.n: Hatband Snatch: little straw hats are yanked off the edge by the band, swinging

p.b1: Wait-and-Swoop: crows strut on the edge, head-bob, then swoop off
p.b2: Black Feather Canopy: long black quills stand up along the edge like a canopy, curving and glinting

b3.n: Two-Aimed Feint: crows split off two ways and hop back, a white glint in the eye

u0.n: Hat Snatch: hats hang at spots tied by a thread; the chain is a crow flying off with one dangling

u1.n: Dive Bomb: a crow dives down the length of the edge with wings tucked, a dark streak behind

u2.n: Mob Caw: gaping crow heads lunge out, caw bursts growing white; rings carry the noise on

u3.n: Glint Eye: crows blink from spot to spot, a white glint flashing in the sly eye

magpie-mob.notes: A noisy gang of black-and-white magpies with long blue-green tails cocking up and down; they chatter and pinch anything shiny.

b0.n: Buckle Sorting Jab: rings and coins are jabbed out of the edge, glinting as they are sorted

b1.n: Noisy Gang Swoop: pied magpies swoop off the edge, tails cocking, chatter clicks

p.b2: Black-White Wing Screen: magpies line the edge, white bellies out, teal tails cocking

b3.n: Borrowed Trinket Dash: the trinkets scatter out and come back, a glint hopping between them

u0.n: Shiny Snatch: a run of rings and coins is swept along the edge in one grab

u1.n: Chatter Guard: magpies scatter out and back chattering, click marks popping

u2.n: Pilfer: trinkets blink from spot to spot as they vanish into the mob

u3.n: Glitter Peck: a magpie darts down the edge pecking, a white sheen flicking off

raven-pair.notes: A huge black raven pair of the high crags, face to face and bowing in turn; hoarse croaking voices, great fingered wings, tough hide.

p.b0: Double-Beak Jab: the pair lunges off the edge, two heavy bills together

b1.n: Crag Drop Talons: the pair drops off the crag edge, scree dust falling

b2.n: Sentry Wing Block: the pair stands sentry along the edge, bowing in turn

b3.n: Talk-Behind Flap: muttering croak arcs scatter out behind and come back

p.u0: Wing Block: one great black wing spreads along the edge, fingered primaries lifting, crag dust
p.u1: Pair Peck: the pair slams out together and drops back

u2.n: Croak Sign: hoarse croak arcs push out like spikes and hold

u3.n: Two Voices: croak arcs hang at spots tied together, two voices answering

jungle-crow.notes: Glossy blue-black rainforest crow with a massive arched bill: a fruit thief that glides out of the canopy and heals on stolen fruit.

b0.n: Fruit-Thief Peck: big glossy bills lunge off the edge and chomp

b1.n: Glossy Talon Drop: the big-billed crow slams down and back, sheen flashing

b2.n: Ink-Black Wing Shade: glossy blue quills stand up along the edge as shade

b3.n: Monkey-Sin Scatter: dropped fruit scatters out and bounces back

u0.n: Canopy Caw: blue crow heads gape and caw bursts lunge off the edge; rings carry the call

u1.n: Fruit Feast: ripe orange fruit rises off the edge, bitten, juice dripping

u2.n: Leaf Mantle: broad leaves scatter out like a mantle and back, the glossy head peeking

p.u3: Bill Snatch: the massive bill chomps down the length of the edge

kestrel-hoverer.notes: Small russet kestrel that hangs dead still in the wind with its tail fanned, wings flickering, then stoops on its prey.

p.b0: Hover Beak Snap: hovering kestrels lunge off the edge, wings flickering

b1.n: Stillness Stoop: kestrels hang, then lunge out of a haze

p.b2: Wind-Hung Wings: grey fanned tails open along the edge like shields

b3.n: Sudden Gust Escape: the kestrels are blown out and come back, gust puffs

u0.n: Hover Drop: kestrels hang over the edge and drop like a stone; the chain hovers then stoops

u1.n: Hang Still: kestrels hang dead still above the edge, only the wings flicker, wind lines streaming

u2.n: Wing Brace: tails fan open along the edge, black band and white tips, dust blown off

u3.n: Wind Stoop: fast kestrels lunge off the edge with a streak behind

cloud-kite.notes: Long-winged red kite with a pale head and deep forked tail riding mountain updrafts and storm fronts; steals food on the wing.

p.b0: Thief Beak Snatch: banking kites lunge off the edge, forked tails twisting

b1.n: Storm-Front Stoop: kites tip and drop off the edge

p.b2: Storm Wing-Fold: pale storm clouds line the edge, rain spots falling

b3.n: Pilfer Flit: kites flit out and back in a haze

u0.n: Gust Buffet: wind curls slam out and drop back, haze above

u1.n: Draught Slip: wind curls hang at spots tied by draught lines

u2.n: Kite Cover: kites spread long wings over the edge and hold, banking slowly

p.u3: Forked Dart: a kite darts the length of the edge, wingtip trails behind

ptarmigan-flock.notes: Round white tundra ptarmigan with a black eye bar and red comb: hides by sinking into the snow, flushes with a whirr, brown in summer.

p.b0: Winter White Peck: white birds lunge off the edge, popping up out of the snow

b1.n: Cross Talon Dive: ptarmigans dive off the edge into the drift

b2.n: Brown Summer Wing: summer-brown ptarmigans line the edge and hold

b3.n: Snowdrift Fade: snow roosts scatter out and back, heads ducking until only red combs show

u0.n: Snow Flurry: white birds burst off the edge in a snow flurry

p.u1: Huddle: snow roosts line the edge, heads poking out; the chain tunnels under the snow

u2.n: Burst Up: white wing-whirr arcs burst out and back as the flock flushes

u3.n: White Scatter: white birds scatter over the snow and sink back in

rock-partridge-covey.notes: Grey rock partridge covey with a black necklace, barred flanks and red legs: runs uphill rather than flies, scratching in mountain and desert grit.

p.b0: Hill Run Peck: running partridges lunge off the edge, red legs pumping

b1.n: Uphill Talon: claw scrapes rake off the edge, grit flung

b2.n: Rock-Grey Wing: grey scree chips line the edge, the covey hidden among them

p.b3: Sprint Uphill: partridges sprint out and back, dust behind
p.u0: Rock Peck: a file of partridges races up the edge, dust behind

u1.n: Scrape Jab: three-groove scrapes shoot along the edge, grit flying

p.u2: Covey Huddle: the covey pushes out heads-first like spikes and holds

u3.n: Uphill Charge: partridges charge out and drop back in a dust cloud; the covey runs on in file

night-heron.notes: Stout hunched night heron with a black cap, glowing red eye and white plume: freezes in the moonlit shallows, then stabs and gulps fish whole.

p.b0: Midnight Stiletto: hunched herons lunge off the edge under the moon, the neck shooting out

b1.n: Hunched Spear Plunge: herons plunge down off the edge, bubbles rising

b2.n: Nightcloak Wings: grey wing hoods mantle out like spikes, red eyes glowing inside

p.b3: Silent Lift Off: herons lift out and settle back under the moon
p.u0: Night Stab: a heron stabs down the length of the edge, red eye leading

u1.n: Stalk Still: herons stand frozen along the edge, only bubbles rise; rings carry on

p.u2: Hooded Wing: wing hoods line the edge, a red eye blinking in the dark of each

u3.n: Gulp Whole: bills lunge out with a silver fish crosswise, then gulp it down

egret-flock.notes: Snow-white egrets with long lacy plumes and yellow dagger bills, wading high-stepping through wetland shallows and following the cattle.

b0.n: Cattle Shadow Jab: egrets lunge off the edge from the cattle's dust

p.b1: Snowy Stalk Strike: tall egrets step out and strike, ripples at their legs
p.b2: Snowplume Canopy: lacy white plumes line the edge and sway
p.b3: Herd Hop Away: egrets scatter out and back
p.u0: Spear Jab: an egret runs the length of the edge, yellow bill first

u1.n: Flock Stab: the flock lunges off the edge one after another, three-toe prints left

p.u2: White Wing Screen: plumes scatter out like a white screen and come back, sheen flecks

u3.n: Stepping Stride: egrets step from spot to spot, prints left in the mud

emu-mob.notes: A mob of a dozen shaggy brown emus with long necks and blue throats: they stampede, kick with huge three-toed feet and raise dust.

p.b0: Shaggy Dream Peck: shaggy emus lunge off the edge, long necks first

b1.n: Stampede Stomp: big three-toed feet slam out and back, prints left

p.b2: Flightless Wing Wall: the mob lines up along the edge, shaggy feathers drifting

b3.n: Mob Scatter Dash: the mob dashes down the edge in a file

u0.n: Kick Stab: a kick shoots down the length of the edge, three toes first, prints left

u1.n: Claw Rake: clawed feet rake off the edge, clods thrown

p.u2: Dust Flurry: emus scatter out and back in a dust cloud
p.u3: Flock Stampede: the mob slams out and drops back; the chain is a stampede file
